title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
text: Section 2(11) defines 'deficiency' as any fault, imperfection, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature and manner of performance which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or has been undertaken to be performed by a person in pursuance of a contract or otherwise in relation to any service. This includes any act of negligence or omission or commission by such person causing loss or injury to the consumer, and deliberate withholding of relevant information by such person to the consumer.

title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
text: Section 2(47) defines 'unfair trade practice' as a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or for the provision of any service, adopts any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice including: falsely representing that goods or services are of a particular standard, quality, quantity, grade, composition, style or model; making false or misleading representations concerning the need for, or the usefulness of, any goods or services; refusing to issue a bill or cash memo; or refusing after delivery of goods or on provision of services to take back or withdraw defective goods or to refund the consideration paid within the period stipulated.

title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
text: Section 34 and 35 empower a consumer to institute a complaint before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission within whose local limits: (a) the opposite party or each of the opposite parties ordinarily resides or carries on business; (b) the cause of action, wholly or in part, arises; or (c) the complainant resides or personally works for gain. The District Commission has pecuniary jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed fifty lakh rupees (updated rules allow up to Rs. 50 Lakhs / 1 Crore).

title: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA)
text: Section 18(1) provides that if the promoter fails to complete or is unable to give possession of an apartment, plot or building in accordance with the terms of the agreement for sale or duly completed by the date specified therein, the promoter shall be liable on demand to the allottees, in case the allottee wishes to withdraw from the project, to return the amount received by him in respect of that apartment, plot, building, with interest at such rate as may be prescribed, including compensation. If the allottee does not withdraw, he shall be paid interest for every month of delay till the handing over of possession.

title: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA)
text: Section 14(3) stipulates that in case any structural defect or any other defect in workmanship, quality or provision of services or any other obligations of the promoter as per the agreement for sale relating to such development is brought to the notice of the promoter within a period of five years by the allottee from the date of handing over possession, it shall be the duty of the promoter to rectify such defects without further charge, within thirty days, and in the event of promoter's failure to rectify such defects within such time, the aggrieved allottees shall be entitled to receive appropriate compensation.

title: Model Tenancy Act / Rent Control Law
text: Section 20 of the Model Tenancy Act prohibits landlords or property managers from withholding or cutting off essential services including water supply, electricity, piped gas, passages, lifts, and sanitation enjoyed by the tenant in the premises without just or sufficient cause, even in the event of non-payment of rent. Under Section 21, no landlord may evict a tenant except by applying to the Rent Authority/Court on specified grounds and serving statutory prior notice.

title: Model Tenancy Act / Rent Control Law
text: Section 10 establishes that the security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall not exceed: (a) two months' rent in the case of residential premises; and (b) six months' rent in the case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant by the landlord after making due deductions of any liability at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises.

title: Right to Information Act, 2005
text: Section 6(1) entitles any citizen to obtain information from a public authority by submitting a request in writing or through electronic means in English or Hindi or in the official language of the area in which the application is being made, accompanied by such fee as prescribed (Rs. 10 under Central rules, free for BPL cardholders). An applicant making request for information shall not be required to give any reason for requesting the information or any other personal details except those that may be necessary for contacting him.

title: Right to Information Act, 2005
text: Section 7(1) mandates that the Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) or State Public Information Officer (SPIO) shall, as expeditiously as possible, and in any case within thirty days of the receipt of the request, either provide the information on payment of such fee as may be prescribed or reject the request for reasons specified in sections 8 and 9. Provided that where the information sought for concerns the life or liberty of a person, the same shall be provided within forty-eight hours of the receipt of the request.

title: Right to Information Act, 2005
text: Section 19(1) provides that any person who, does not receive a decision within thirty days (or 48 hours for life and liberty), or is aggrieved by a decision of the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, may within thirty days from the expiry of such period or from the receipt of such a decision prefer an appeal to such officer who is senior in rank to the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer as the First Appellate Authority (FAA).

title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
text: Section 12 allows an aggrieved woman or a Protection Officer to present an application to the Magistrate seeking one or more reliefs under this Act, including protection orders under Section 18 prohibiting acts of domestic violence, residence orders under Section 19 securing right to reside in shared household, monetary relief under Section 20, and compensation under Section 22. Emergency assistance is available through Women Helpline 181 and Police 112.

title: Information Technology Act, 2000 & BNS (Cyber Financial Fraud)
text: Section 66D of the Information Technology Act penalizes cheating by personation by using computer resource with imprisonment up to three years. For unauthorized UPI transfers, OTP phishing, or credit card fraud, immediate reporting on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) or dialling helpline 1930 within the 'Golden Hour' allows law enforcement and banks to freeze fraudulent transaction accounts before the money is withdrawn.

title: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
text: Section 12 gives every person who has to file or defend a case the right to free legal services under this Act if that person is: (a) a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe; (b) a victim of trafficking in human beings or begar; (c) a woman or a child; (d) a person with disability; (e) a person under circumstances of underserved want; or (f) in receipt of annual income less than the state threshold (typically Rs. 3 Lakhs per annum). Citizens can approach their District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or call NALSA Helpline 15100.

title: Fortune Infrastructure & Anr. v. Trevor D'Lima
text: The Supreme Court of India held that a flat purchaser or homebuyer cannot be expected to wait indefinitely for possession of the allotted flat. Where there is an inordinate delay in handing over possession, the buyer is entitled to seek a full refund of the amount paid along with reasonable interest and compensation. The developer cannot compel the buyer to accept delayed possession or alternative flats not agreed upon in the primary contract.

title: National Seeds Corp. Ltd. v. M. Madhusudhan Reddy
text: The Supreme Court affirmed that the remedies provided under the Consumer Protection Act are in addition to and not in derogation of any other law for the time being in force. An aggrieved person is free to elect the forum of the Consumer Commission even if other dispute resolution or statutory arbitration mechanisms exist, provided the claim meets the test of deficiency of service or unfair trade practice.

title: CBSE & Anr. v. Aditya Bandopadhyay & Ors.
text: The Supreme Court held that an examining body (such as CBSE or Universities) does not hold evaluated answer books in a fiduciary relationship with the examiner or candidate. An examinee has the fundamental right under the RTI Act to inspect and obtain copies of their evaluated answer sheets, subject only to redaction of the examiner's identity to ensure their safety and neutrality.
